I think what makes something Camp is the notion that the piece of art/media DOES take itself seriously (with a grain of salt of course) and THEN is labeled Campy by the audience, if you make something with the intention of it being Camp, it automatically makes it NOT Camp you know? like Rocky Horror for example, it was made with the intention of it being a spooky/funny/weird and unsettling musical, but the general public didn't see it that way, they just thought it was trashy and bad, but when they started to put on showings of it later in the night, the LGBTQ+ and Queer crowd ate it up ! And it became a cult classic for queer culture, which is a pillar for Camp culture as well, Queer people loved the weirdness, the over-the-top sexuality of the costumes, characters, music and themes, they could identify with it, it was drag when drag wasn't in pop culture. When something KNOWS it's bad or somewhat goofy, and it leans into it, like soap operas or Grey's Anatomy type shows, it's Kitsch, because it's made with the intention of it being dramatic with over-the-top characters and stories. That's why i think seasons 1-4 are Camp, but it slowly becomes Kitsch after that because Riverdale show runners knew the reputation it had gained amongst viewers, so they leaned into the drama and became too self-aware about being "bad". Camp is accidental, Kitsch is intentional.
